runs.content:
**Investigation idea:** Burry's Freddie Mac (FMCC) long thesis explicitly rests on two of his own named source posts that were never ingested into the wiki. finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-08-07.md's own Freddie Mac section states the FMCC long is a "Continuation of a thesis Burry has run since December 2025 ('Fannie & Freddie, Toxic Twins No More No More,' not yet filed in this wiki) and updated a month ago in 'Fannie, Freddie, Trump & The Housing Crisis' (also not yet filed)." Both posts are explicitly named as the actual underlying argument for a real, disclosed Burry position already propagated into finance/morningstar/morningstar-watchlist.md's Burry Longs table — but the wiki only holds the truncated Aug 7 trade summary, not the full thesis those two posts would supply. Next step: locate and ingest both named source posts as dedicated source pages, cross-linked from source-burry-trading-post-2026-08-07.md and finance/michael-burry/trading-posts.md.

**Cross-domain connection:** Finance just added Taiwan Semiconductor to its watchlist on a one-line "AI/HPC volume growth thesis" — AI & Tech already has the fully-worked structural research behind that exact thesis, uncited. finance/morningstar/morningstar-watchlist.md added TSM (2026-08-05 screen) at FV $534 / 27% discount, described only as "~70% foundry market share; AI/HPC volume growth thesis." AI & Tech already has extensive, dated research on exactly this company: ai-tech/data-tsmc-cowos-2026-06-27.md documents CoWoS packaging as TSMC's own single point of failure (NVIDIA has locked >50% of capacity), ai-tech/model-ai-ecosystem-constraint-edges-2026-06-27.md ranks TSMC Tier 1 in its own investment-signal ranking, and ai-tech/source-tsmc-100b-us-investment-ai-demand-2026-07-19.md shows TSMC itself raising 2026 capex guidance to $60–64B and revenue growth guidance to >40% specifically on AI demand — a direct confirming data point for the Morningstar thesis, three weeks before it was added to the watchlist. Neither side cross-links the other. Next step: add a line to the TSM watchlist row citing the CoWoS constraint-edge model and the $100B investment source, and add a reverse link from data-tsmc-cowos-2026-06-27.md's See Also to the Morningstar watchlist.

**Cross-domain connection:** Books' own unread Peter Lynch case study is literally the origin story of the modern position Burry just added — the same company family, the same turnaround pattern, forty years apart. books/book-lynch-beating-the-street.md (aspirational, unread) dedicates its centrepiece chapter to a "Turnaround Master Class" on Fannie Mae: bought near-insolvent in the early-1980s S&L crisis via a 4-step process (survival check on the implicit government guarantee, business-quality read on its securitisation monopoly, new-management assessment, deep discount to book value), becoming a 30-bagger for Magellan. finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-08-07.md documents Burry's new Freddie Mac (FMCC) long — Fannie Mae's sister GSE — built on a near-identical structural argument: book value compounding regardless of conservatorship/IPO timing, sentiment-driven weakness framed as a buying opportunity for patient holders. Neither page cites the other, and the book isn't on books/reading-list.md yet. Next step: add the book to reading-list.md's aspirational section — Lynch's own 4-step framework is a ready-made lens for testing whether Burry's FMCC thesis repeats the 30-bagger setup or is a case where post-2008 GSE conservatorship makes "this time different."

Monday focus (Finance + Crypto): deep-read Finance's post-08-08 additions (4 new Morningstar source pages, the Aug 7 Burry trading post, the RELX/ZTS/LULU/MELI magic-formula + technical-analyst batch, the growth-value-tracker's first spread-compression-of-the-year read) and Crypto's current state (no new content since the 08-08 portfolio refresh — crypto-overview.md still stale since 2026-05-01, already covered by open threads). The magic-formula batch turned out to already be thoroughly cross-linked internally (Burry context + TA verdict + Morningstar FV sit side-by-side per stock), so connection budget went to two genuinely fresh, unlinked pairings instead. No items resolved this run.

**Investigation idea:** The Bank of America AI-upskilling episode that ai-future-of-work.md was waiting for now exists as an actual page with concrete findings — and still hasn't been used. On 2026-07-23 this log flagged that "Me, Myself, and AI"'s BofA reskilling episode recommendation was a ready primary source for ai-tech/ai-future-of-work.md's unresolved "Is there a policy response that actually works?" question. Today's podcast-summarizer catch-up run created podcasts/podcast-me-myself-and-ai-bank-of-america-bernard-hampton.md, confirming Fred has now actually listened — the episode covers BofA's Bernard Hampton running "The Academy," upskilling 200,000+ employees through 1,000+ facilitators via an explicit three-level AI-adoption framework, with defined rules for where humans must stay in the loop. ai-future-of-work.md's own Open Questions section is unchanged — still asks the retraining/policy question purely in the abstract, with zero mention of Hampton, BofA, or any employer case study. This advances rather than resolves the 2026-07-23 idea — the precondition (Fred listening) is now met, but the actual cross-link still hasn't happened. Next step: pull Hampton's three-level framework and human-in-the-loop boundaries into ai-future-of-work.md's Open Questions as the first concrete employer case study.

**Cross-domain connection:** A podcast newly ingested today independently tests the exact thesis behind Fred's own live Wolters Kluwer position, three days after he opened it. finance/trading-portfolio.md shows WKL initiated 2026-08-05 with an explicit thesis: "recurring professional information revenue; no AI infrastructure exposure; Grantham-aligned non-US quality." podcasts/podcast-dividend-talk-q2-2026-earnings-season.md — created today by the podcast-summarizer catch-up run — devotes a full segment to exactly this question: "why IBM crashed 25% while RELX, Wolters Kluwer, and Texas Instruments pushed back against the AI-doom narrative." A real market-data test of the specific "no AI infrastructure exposure" bet Fred made three days before the episode's content would have reached him, sitting in a completely different domain from the position itself. Neither page currently cites the other. Next step: add a line to trading-portfolio.md's WKL thesis note citing this episode's IBM-vs-RELX/WKL/TXN resilience framing as an early real-world signal.

**Cross-domain connection:** Gavin Baker's newest podcast claims he spent a week hunting for a negative AI data point and found none — the wiki itself built one the very next day. podcasts/podcast-invest-like-the-best-gavin-baker-ai-market-jitters.md has Baker describing "spending a week deliberately hunting for a single negative quantitative data point about AI demand or spend and coming up empty," framed as a numbers-first rebuttal of the AI-bubble narrative. finance/models/model-oracle-cashflow-debt-rpo-2026-08-07.md — built the day after this episode was added to the wiki — is exactly that kind of number, company-specific: Oracle's FY2026 free cash flow at −$23.7bn, debt roughly doubled in 21 months to $129.5bn, a credit downgrade to BBB−, and CDS spreads at an 18-year high, with a bear case showing a $10–15bn financing gap — corroborated the same week by Michael Burry's fresh ORCL short. Not a direct rebuttal (Baker's claim is about aggregate demand, not one company's balance sheet), but exactly the class of concrete negative number his framing implies doesn't exist. Next step: add a line to Baker's podcast page's "Why Notable" section noting the Oracle model as a company-specific counterpoint.

Saturday full sweep: skimmed memory/index.md's Domain Content Status and index.md's master catalog across all domains, then focused on log.md's post-08-07 diff — a new Oracle cashflow/debt model (finance/models/, 2026-08-07) and six podcast pages newly created today by a podcast-summarizer catch-up run backfilling episodes that were 'Completed — listened' but never had wiki pages (Gavin Baker AI Market Jitters, Alex Hormozi Stop Chasing AI, Ray Dalio 2008-crash/AI-bubble, Me Myself and AI × BofA, Business Breakdown Toast/Auto1, Dividend Talk Q2 earnings). The three new AI-bubble-adjacent podcast pages (Baker/Dalio/Hormozi) already cross-link each other within Podcasts, so connection budget went to the two genuinely cross-domain, unlinked pairs instead. No items resolved this run.
